pr.title: Give field keys knobs: choose with the arrows, turn with up and down, and map them through each instrument's knob file (instrument-knobs.md chunk 1)
pr.head: 6a7f2a299257ec425f723d61cd44debd0648071e

summary: field keys plays music from the computer keyboard. It publishes a virtual MIDI source named Field Keys, and when you name an instrument, such as field keys juno in examples/bloom, it also starts a voice host: a SuperCollider process that turns each MIDI note into a voice of that instrument. Until now the only thing you could change about the sound while playing was the modulation wheel (MIDI controller 1), in six fixed steps on keys 3 to 8.

This pull request is chunk 1 of the instrument-knobs plan. It gives field keys knobs, the way a hardware MIDI controller has them. An instrument describes its knobs in a knob file beside its program, juno.knobs.yaml beside juno.scd. Each knob names a MIDI controller (a CC, a numbered control-change message), a range, a curve, and a default. A new knob line above the status line shows every knob. The left and right arrows choose a knob, and up and down turn it, faster the longer you hold. Every turn leaves field keys as an ordinary control change on Field Keys, so any instrument can answer it and a recorded take keeps it.

On the SuperCollider side, the voicer, the shared code that turns MIDI into voices both live and when a take renders, now hands every controller from 2 to 119 except sustain to the voices as a control named for its number, such as cc74, from 0 to 1. A voice maps that control to its own parameter. juno and bass map four knobs each through their knob file, read from a checked copy that Field writes after the file passes its schema and names in the FIELD_KNOBS environment variable. So a voice never reads a file Field rejected.

musical, a new built-in keymap, replaces musical-typing as the default. It keeps every note and the octave, velocity, and sustain keys, puts the knobs on the arrows, and moves the pitch bend to , and .. Typing a knob's value on the number row, gliding to it, and a take that starts where your knobs are come in chunks 2 and 3.

Read the open review finding first. A knob file that passes the schema but leaves out one of the four knobs juno.scd or bass.scd maps, as the plan's own criterion 11 does, makes that instrument's voice fail to load, live and in a take's render.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Controller (CC): a MIDI control-change message, numbered 0 to 127, with a value from 0 to 127. CC 1 is the modulation wheel, CC 64 the sustain pedal, CC 74 usually a filter's cutoff.
  • Knob file: a YAML file, <program>.knobs.yaml, listing an instrument's knobs: name, cc, min, max, curve (lin or exp), step, units, and default.
  • Knob line: the line between the instrument's line and the status line that shows every knob's name and value, the chosen one in reverse video.
  • Voice host: the sclang process sc/voice-host.scd that plays an instrument live.
  • Voicer: sc/voicer.scd, which turns MIDI into voices for both the voice host and a take's render.
  • Voice mode: an instrument program run with FIELD_MODE=voice, whose value is one playable voice (a SynthDef) rather than a rendered file.
  • Checked copy: the copy of a knob file that Field writes after the file passes the schema, with every field filled in, and names in FIELD_KNOBS.
  • Take: a recorded MIDI performance on a track. Its render plays the take through the instrument offline to produce audio.

cards.title: What chunk 1 covers
cards.html:
• In this pull request: knob files and --knobs, the knob line, choosing and turning, musical as the default, the voicer's cc<n>, the checked copies, the render's check and cache input, field check, juno and bass, and the docs. Acceptance criteria 1 to 3, 9 to 11, 13, 15 to 17, 19, and 22, and 12 and 18 up to their typed values.
  • Chunk 2: typing a value on the number row, Enter, Backspace, Period as the decimal point, Esc cancelling instead of quitting, and the glide. Criteria 4 to 8, 14, and 23.
  • Chunk 3: a take that starts where your knobs were, through .field/keys.json and the daemon's controller chase. Criteria 20 and 21.
  • Still open: the plan's §3.2 recommends that voices read the checked copy, so each range is written once, and records that Justin has not ruled on it. This pull request builds on the recommendation.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One review, at 6a7f2a2, with one open finding: a knob file without one of the four knobs juno.scd maps stops its voice from loading.
  • The head was reviewed by reading only. Both commits carry a Co-Authored-By: Claude trailer that GitHub attributes to the login claude, which has read access only, so the review ran none of the head's code.
  • CI passes on this head. The windows job failed on the first head, b4be562, on the --knobs path test, which the second commit fixes.

groups.title: The knob file and what a controller value means
groups.kicker: One zod schema checks every knob file, and one module maps, steps, and prints knob values.
intro: A knob file lists an instrument's knobs. src/schema/knobs.ts is the only check of one, and every path that hands a knob file to an instrument runs it first: field keys at start and on each save, and a take's render in its validate, which is also how field check reports a bad file.

src/keys/knobs.ts holds everything else about knobs that does not depend on a terminal. It finds an instrument's knob file beside its program, resolves --knobs, reads and watches files, and converts between a controller value from 0 to 127 and the knob's value. That conversion is SuperCollider's ControlSpec.map for the curve of the same name, so a voice that maps with ControlSpec plays what the line shows. It also prints each value at a fixed width, so turning one knob never moves the knobs after it.

checks.text: A lin knob spreads the 128 controller values evenly over its range, and an exp knob by equal ratios, which suits a frequency or a time. That is why the schema rejects an exp range that touches or crosses 0.

files.note: The knob file's schema: field defaults, then a superRefine for the rules that span knobs (free controllers, unique names and controllers, exp ranges, default inside the range).

checks.text: An exp knob whose min or max is 0, or whose ends differ in sign, is rejected, and the default check uses Math.min and Math.max of the ends, so both ends are inside and a downward range works. Read against plan §2.2.
Nothing ties step to the range. With min: 0, max: 1, step: 0.4, the top controller value rounds to 1.2, past max, on the line and in ControlSpec alike. The review lists this as a suggestion.

files.note: Finding knob files, reading and watching them, writing the checked copy, mapping between controller values and knob values, stepping, and printing at a fixed width.

checks.text: The width rule gives mod 0 cutoff 2.00 kHz res 0.300 attack 800 ms release 1.50 s for juno's defaults: widths 3, 8, 5, 7, and 7, the widest each knob prints at its default or any of its 128 values. Worked by hand from formatKnobValue and significant.
The checked copy is the schema's output, so it has every field with defaults filled. A voice never needs to know the schema's defaults, and a knob file may leave out step, as juno.knobs.yaml does.
KnobsError, parseKnobs, loadKnobs, and watchKnobs follow src/keys/keymap.ts's keymap loader almost line for line. The review suggests one shared helper.

groups.title: Choosing and turning in the keys session
groups.kicker: The session keeps every controller it sent, the knob list and the choice, and times a held turn key itself.
intro: KeysSession in src/keys/session.ts turns key presses into MIDI messages and has no terminal or timer of its own. Two new keymap actions reach it: { knob: n } moves the choice n knobs, wrapping past either end, and { turn: n } turns the chosen knob n steps. A step is one controller value, or for a knob with a step, the next controller value that maps to a different value.

The session now records every controller it sends in one map, by number. The modulation wheel's old mod field becomes a read of controller 1 in that map, and a knob that has not been turned starts from its default's controller value. A held turn key turns again on each 40 ms tick(now), faster the longer it is held, and the caller passes the time in, so tests run the acceleration without waiting.

checks.text: A held turn moves 1 step at the press, none before 300 ms, then 1 step a tick to 1 s, 2 to 1.5 s, and 4 after, so 0 to 127 takes about 2.32 s, matching plan §2.6. Each tick sends at most one control change, so at most 25 a second. Walked tick by tick from TURN_RATES.

files.note: The controller map, the knob list and the choice, knob and turn actions, tick, and setKnobs for a saved knob file.

checks.text: Release of the turn key, focus-out and panic (both through releaseAll), and quit all clear the held turn, so tick returns nothing after them. A second turn key replaces the first, and releasing the first does not stop the second.
A new knob list keeps each knob's value, because values live in the controller map by number, and keeps the choice on the knob with the same label, or the nearest index when that knob is gone.
setsMod() still asks the keymap whether a key can move the wheel. The plan's §2.9 and §3 say it becomes a read of the controller map, so the review suggests recording the difference in §9.1.

files.note: Adds the knob and turn actions, each a non-zero whole number.

Renamed from musical-typing.yaml. The bend moves from 1 and 2 to Comma and Period, the wheel's steps on 3 to 8 go, and the arrows choose and turn knobs. The number row stays free for chunk 2's typing.

checks.text: tracker and fourths are unchanged, so they bind no knob action and show no knob line (criterion 15).

files.note: DEFAULT_KEYMAP becomes musical. A bare --keymap musical-typing now fails as any unknown built-in does.
field keys --print tags the actions K-1, K+1, R+1, and R-1, and describes each.

checks.text: "choose the knob 1 to the right" can read as knob number 1. The review suggests "move the choice 1 knob to the right".

groups.title: The voicer hands every controller to the voices
groups.kicker: SuperCollider's side knows nothing about knobs: each controller becomes a control named for its number.
intro: The voicer already kept the modulation wheel's last value and set it on every voice as mod. It now does the same for every controller from 2 to 119 except the sustain pedal, as cc2 to cc119, each from 0 to 1, keeping one value per controller across all channels. A new voice starts with every stored value, and a sounding voice gets each change. scsynth ignores a control a voice does not have, so an instrument answers only the controllers it names.

The voice host now receives FIELD_INSTRUMENTS as a list of objects, each with the program's path and, when it has a knob file, the path of its checked copy. voice-load.scd sets or unsets FIELD_KNOBS for each program just before running it, so one program's copy never leaks into the next.

files.note: Stores controllers in an IdentityDictionary and passes them to start as a list, such as [\mod, 0.5, \cc74, 1.0].

checks.text: The case tests 64 and 123 before the 1-to-119 range, so sustain and All Notes Off keep their meaning and never become controls. Controller 0 and 120 to 127 match no branch. Read in order.

files.note: Reads each instrument's program and knobs from the objects, and appends the voicer's controls to each new synth's arguments.
Takes the copy's path beside the program's, and sets or unsets FIELD_KNOBS before it runs the program.

checks.text: The variable is set or unset on every call, so in a host that loads juno and then pad, pad runs with FIELD_KNOBS unset.

files.note: Builds FIELD_INSTRUMENTS as objects, with knobs only for a program that has a checked copy.

groups.title: A take's render checks and hashes the knob file
groups.kicker: The knob file now decides how a take sounds, so the build checks it, keys the cache on it, and hands the voice its own checked copy.
intro: A take on a track whose record entry names an instrument renders through the voice-render generator, which runs the same voicer offline. Because juno's voice now maps its controls through its knob file, editing that file must render the take again.

The generator's validate runs the knob file through the schema, so a bad file fails field check and the build with the schema's errors before sclang runs. The file joins the render's cache inputs when it exists. The render writes its own checked copy beside the events file and names it in FIELD_KNOBS, and it refuses to cache when the knob file changed while it ran, as it already refused for the program.

files.note: Checks the knob file in validate, adds it to extraInputs, writes and removes the copy around the run, and compares its hash in verifyAfterRun.

checks.text: The after-run check compares the file's hash, or its absence, with the input recorded before the run, so an edit, a deletion, or a file created during the render each refuse the cache.

files.note: Passes FIELD_KNOBS to voice-load.scd and appends the voicer's controls to each s_new.
Pins that field check reports a record entry whose instrument's knob file fails the schema.

groups.title: juno and bass map four knobs each
groups.kicker: The example instruments read their checked copy and put four knobs in place of fixed settings.
intro: juno.scd and bass.scd keep their sound in a settings Event that the JU-06A voice function reads. In voice mode they now replace four settings, the filter's cutoff and resonance and the envelope's attack and release, with signals from their knobs. A small knob helper finds each knob by name in the checked copy and maps cc74 and the others through a ControlSpec built from the copy, starting at the knob's default. Settings the voice tests with if, such as chorusOn, stay fixed.

The render branch, which field sc render runs outside voice mode, is unchanged, so its output keeps its bytes (criterion 19). The knob files use General MIDI 2's sound controllers, 71 to 74, so a hardware controller set up for General MIDI turns the same knobs.

files.note: The voice branch reads FIELD_KNOBS, throws a clear error when it is unset, and maps four knobs through the copy.

checks.text: Open finding: knob indexes the result of knobs.detect without checking it. A knob file that passes the schema but lacks attack, as after criterion 11's first save, makes the SynthDef build throw Message 'at' not understood. The reload fails, the next field keys juno cannot start the voice, and a take's render fails while field check passes. The fix the finding names is to fall back to the setting's fixed value when the copy has no knob of that name.
This comment, the one in bass.scd, and both knob files cite a "Knobs" section of docs/keys.md that does not exist. The sections are "Knob files" and "Make an instrument playable".

files.note: The same helper and the same four knobs as juno, with bass's defaults.

checks.text: The same lookup as juno.scd's open finding: a knob file without one of the four knobs stops bass's voice from loading.

files.note: juno's four knobs: cutoff on CC 74, resonance on 71, attack on 73, and release on 72.
The same four knobs with bass's defaults: 1200 Hz, 0.4, 5 ms, and 150 ms.

groups.title: field keys draws the knob line and keeps the copies
groups.kicker: The command reads every knob file before it starts, owns the checked copies, runs the turn timer, and redraws the lines above the status line.
intro: field keys checks every knob file before anything starts, as it checks the keymap: an armed instrument's file beside its program, and each --knobs file. A bare --knobs name means shared/instruments/<name>.knobs.yaml in the project, and anything with a / or ending in .yaml is a path.

KnobFiles owns the sources and the checked copies, in a temporary directory removed when the session ends, a throw included. When a watched knob file is saved, a file that passes replaces that source's knobs and rewrites the copy before the voice reloads. A file that fails changes only the status line, which then reads knobs not reloaded: with the first error. The voice keeps its last good copy, including when you save the program itself while its knob file is failing.

The knob line appears when the keymap binds a knob action, and the status line then leaves out its mod field. KnobLine pads each value to its fixed width, shows the chosen knob in reverse video, and on a narrow terminal shows a window of whole knobs that moves only when the choice leaves it. redrawAbove rewrites the lines above the status line from the first one that changed.

files.note: Loads knob sources, owns the copies in KnobFiles, watches knob files, runs the 40 ms turn timer only while a turn key is held, and draws the knob line.

checks.text: A failing save records its error and returns false, so the watcher reloads no voice and the copy is untouched. A passing save rewrites every copy that reads the file before it returns true and the voice reloads.
The copies' directory is removed in the finally that closes the routing, so it goes on a normal quit, a signal, and a throw from inside the session.
The interval starts when a turn key is held and is cleared after the input that releases it, after a focus-out, and after quit, so a session with no turn held keeps no timer.

On a terminal narrower than about 25 columns, the chosen knob's cell plus the ‹ and › markers can exceed the width, the line wraps, and the redraw's cursor-up count no longer matches the screen. The review suggests slicing the cell to the width left after the markers.

files.note: Adds the repeatable --knobs option and names musical as the default keymap in --keymap's help.

groups.title: Docs and plans
groups.kicker: keys.md gains knobs and musical, build-graph.md the cc<n> controls and the knob file as a render input, and the plan its as-built section.
intro: docs/keys.md gains a "Turn knobs" section with "Knob files" and "Knobs for another instrument", describes musical as the default with Logic's number row as controls to copy, and adds cc<n> and FIELD_KNOBS to the voice contract under "Make an instrument playable". Esc still quits, which stays true until chunk 2.

The instrument-knobs plan moves to in-progress and now, and gains §9, which records what implementation settled and what was verified. The keyboard-instrument plan gets a dated note at §3, where it chose Musical Typing as the default.
